keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for this regime. The page: the government 'nominally controlled the provinces of Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan and Jiangsu' (Jiangsu belongs to the Reformed Government next door; the Reformed Government page assigns it Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, so Jiangsu is not drawn here). The East Hebei zone is cut out because the East Hebei Autonomous Council 'continued to resist fully integrating' until February 1938. 'Nominally': the Japanese army held the towns and rail lines, and Mengjiang's and the South Chahar and North Shanxi governments' zones overlap Chahar and north Shanxi. No infobox area. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F173: the south-western corner of Shanxi is subtracted. Yan Xishan page (opened 2026-11-01): 'As the Japanese invasion pushed Yan's administration into the southwest corner of Shanxi, he established a base there'; the Provisional Government page (opened 2026-11-01): the regime 'nominally controlled the provinces of Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan and Jiangsu' but 'its real influence was largely limited to where Japanese military control extended permanently', which did not include Yan's base. The ring is the one of shanxi-clique_1938 (110.2-112.6 E, 34.6-36.6 N), cut to Shanxi.]

region.text: Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi and Henan (nominal), capital Beijing

ledger.note: 14 December 1937: the government is inaugurated by Wang Kemin 'on 14 December 1937, with its capital at Beijing', 'formed largely on the initiative of Imperial Japanese Army commanders in north China'. The provinces are what it 'nominally controlled'; the page names no counties and says its authority was 'further limited' by the Inner Mongolian autonomous government. The Reformed Government page gives the same founding as 'from December 1937'.

region.text: the East Hebei zone, 22 counties between Beijing and Tianjin and the Great Wall

ledger.note: February 1938: 'absorbed into the collaborationist Provisional Government of China in February 1938' (East Hebei page, no day). The Provisional Government page lists the East Hebei Autonomous Government among its preceding entities and says East Hebei 'continued to resist fully integrating', without a date.

region.text: all of the Provisional Government's land

ledger.note: 30 March 1940: 'merged into Wang Jingwei's Nanjing-based reorganized national government on 30 March 1940'; it 'stayed virtually independent' as the North China Political Council 'until the end of the war'. The land does not change hands in practice.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The regime was a Japanese creation ('formed largely on the initiative of Imperial Japanese Army commanders') and lasted to the merger of 30 March 1940.
wars.note: The war itself was not opened for this dossier; the Republic of China and Empire of Japan dossiers carry the Japanese occupation of North China as their own occupation events.

certainty.note: A nominal claim on four provinces: the Japanese army held the towns and lines, the page gives no counties, and the Mengjiang, South Chahar and North Shanxi zones overlap.

sources.title: Provisional Government of the Republic of China (1937-1940)
sources.note: Founding 14 December 1937 at Beijing; nominal provinces; merger 30 March 1940 into the Reorganized National Government; Wang Kemin; silent on area, on East Hebei's absorption date and on Qingdao.

sources.title: East Hebei Autonomous Council
sources.note: Absorbed into the Provisional Government in February 1938; 22 counties.

sources.title: Yan Xishan
sources.note: 'As the Japanese invasion pushed Yan's administration into the southwest corner of Shanxi, he established a base there where he lived in sparse conditions for eight years' (the south-west corner stayed outside the Japanese-sponsored governments).

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from two pages (a 2.3-year state, below the ten-year bar, written because the East Hebei, Mengjiang and Reorganized-government dossiers name it as a counterpart). Not settled: (1) the page's list of provinces includes Jiangsu, which the Reformed Government page gives to the Reformed Government; not drawn. (2) The page is silent on Qingdao and Tianjin's status beyond a 'Tianjin Special City' mayor, so Beijing and Tianjin are drawn with the four provinces. (3) The page gives no area or population. (4) Overlap: Mengjiang's Zhangjiakou and Datong zones (from 1939) and the South Chahar and North Shanxi governments (no dossier; the Mengjiang page names them) lie inside the drawn provinces; the compile step should draw Mengjiang over this state. (5) The Republic of China (ea-08-c) and Empire of Japan (jk-01-d) dossiers carry this land as Japanese occupation from 1937-1938 and have no event naming this state; a reviewer should decide whether to add a loss for the Republic and a vassal_start for Japan. The merger of 30 March 1940 changed no border (North China Political Council); the successor's dossier is reorganized-national-government-of-china.
